papers.title: Parabolic Rectifiable Reifenberg for Measures
papers.abstract: We announce a structure theory for measures on $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ equipped with the parabolic distance. Our results include a parabolic rectifiable Reifenberg theorem for arbitrary Radon measures, qualitative and quantitative characterizations of regular parabolic rectifiability by Jones square functions, and sharp results for $L^p$ beta numbers. The results hold in every parabolic dimension and extend the theories of Edelen--Naber--Valtorta, Azzam--Tolsa and David--Semmes to space-time. The stated theorems and corollaries, together with their proofs, are formalized in Lean~4 with Mathlib.

papers.title: Symbolic Integration of Differential Forms: From Abel to Zeilberger
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on symbolic integration of differential forms, with a particular emphasis on historical and modern developments, from Abel's addition theorems for Abelian integrals to Zeilberger's creative telescoping for parameterized integrals. It explores closed rational $p$-forms and provides algorithmic approaches for their integration, extending classical results like Hermite reduction and Liouville's theorem. The integration of closed differential forms with parameters is further examined through telescopers, offering a unified framework for handling both algebraic and transcendental cases.

papers.title: Fourier quasicrystals with positive integer masses are sections of Lee-Yang cycles
papers.abstract: We prove that Fourier quasicrystal measures with positive integer masses are precisely the nonzero real sections of effective Lee-Yang cycles by matrices with positive maximal minors, with masses given by weighted local intersection degrees. For Delone support, the reduced support of the cycle can be chosen strict. For unit masses, the cycle can be chosen reduced, with local intersection degree one at every root. Every integer-mass FQ measure has support equal to the common complex zero set of finitely many real-valued trigonometric polynomials. These results answer Questions (1), (2), and (4) of Alon, Kummer, Kurasov, and Vinzant. We recover a finite-dimensional torus from the spectrum and prove that its canonical analytic set is algebraic. A support-height theorem for holonomic sequences provides a linear spectral bound, from which we reconstruct the complex branches and their integer coefficients using fiber moments. Singular sections carry their natural local intersection degrees; discarding these can destroy the Fourier quasicrystal property.

papers.title: Extremal cosine sign correlations
papers.abstract: We prove that four cosines with distinct positive integer frequencies have the same sign on at least $1/33$ of a period, with equality precisely for positive integer dilates of $\{1,3,11,33\}$. If both odd and even frequencies occur, the optimal proportion is $1/24$; equality holds precisely for odd positive integer dilates of $\{1,3,4,12\}$ and $\{2,4,5,15\}$. For arbitrary $n$, we establish the universal lower bound $4^{1-n}$ and construct frequency sets for which this proportion is at most $16n^\theta4^{-n}$, where $\theta=\log_2(3/2)$. These bounds determine the optimal exponential decay rate $1/4$.

papers.title: On the positive Lebesgue measure of (n,k,t)-sets
papers.abstract: We study sets in R^n that contain a unit k-dimensional disk in each direction from a subset of the Grassmannian G(n,k) of Hausdorff dimension at least t; we call them (n,k,t)-sets. In the range 2k>n, we prove that every (n,k,t)-set has positive Lebesgue measure whenever t>k(n-k-1)+1. This follows from a sharp Sobolev-to-L^2 estimate for the k-plane maximal operator over a Frostman measure on G(n,k), which also yields an L^p-L^2 estimate for every p>n/k with respect to Haar measure. In the range 2k<=n, where translations can no longer be ignored, we obtain the same threshold via a lifting argument, conditional on the quantitative Kakeya estimate in dimension n-k+1. Using the quantitative Kakeya estimate of Wang and Zahl in dimension 3, we deduce that (4,2,t)-sets have positive measure for t>3. The threshold t>k(n-k-1)+1 is sharp, in the sense that (n,k,t)-sets of measure zero exist at t=k(n-k-1)+1. These results improve the previous threshold t>n/2+k(n-k-1) of Fraser, Harris and Kroon, and give the first restricted-direction results in the range 2k<=n.

papers.title: The endpoints $p_-=1$ and $p_+=\infty$ for the maximal operator on $L^{p(\cdot)}$ over spaces of homogeneous type
papers.abstract: We investigate the boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $M$ on variable Lebesgue spaces $L^{p(\cdot)}(\Omega,d,\mu)$ over spaces of homogeneous type, focusing on the endpoints $p_-=1$ and $p_+=\infty$. At the lower endpoint, we prove that the boundedness of $M$ forces $p_->1$ for all exponents if and only if the space $(\Omega,d,\mu)$ is non-atomic. At the upper endpoint, we generalize the Muckenhoupt-Nekvinda sufficient condition of Adamadze, Diening, and Kopaliani. On bounded spaces of homogeneous type, whenever $p_->1$, this yields a boundedness criterion based on the Muckenhoupt condition alone. We also construct an unbounded space where the Muckenhoupt condition suffices for the maximal operator's boundedness.

papers.title: Sharp Quantitative Weighted Estimates for Lifted Maximal Operators with Applications
papers.abstract: In this article, we establish sharp quantitative weighted estimates for the lifted Hardy--Littlewood (resp Sobolev sharp) maximal operators $\{\mathcal M_\theta\}_{\theta\in(0,\infty)}$ (resp $\{\mathcal M_\theta^\sharp\}_{\theta\in(0,\infty)}$). Specifically, for $p\in(1,\infty)$, $\gamma\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, $\upsilon\in A_p$, and $f\in L^p_\upsilon$, we prove that \begin{align*} \sup_{\theta,\lambda\in(0,\infty)}\lambda^p \underset{\mathcal M_\theta(f)(x,t)>\lambda t^\gamma} {\int_{\mathbb R^n}\int_0^\infty} t^{\gamma p-1}\,dt\,\upsilon(x)\,dx \lesssim [\upsilon]_{A_p}^{\alpha_{p,\gamma}} \|f\|_{L^p_\upsilon}^p, \end{align*} where $\alpha_{p,\gamma}:=\frac{p}{p-1}$ for $\gamma\in[-n,0)$ and $\alpha_{p,\gamma}:=1$ otherwise and where the implicit positive constant depends only on $n$, $p$, and $\gamma$. For $\mathcal M_\theta^\sharp$, the corresponding estimate holds with $\|f\|_{L^p_\upsilon}^p$ replaced by $\|\nabla f\|_{L^p_\upsilon}^p$ for any $f\in\dot W^{1,p}_\upsilon$, and with $\alpha_{p,\gamma}:=\frac{p}{p-1}$ for $\gamma\in[-1,0)$ and $\alpha_{p,\gamma}:=1$ otherwise. We show that, for an $A_1$ weight $\upsilon$, the weight constant in the above estimates becomes $[\upsilon]_{A_1}$ for the sharp ranges $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $\gamma\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, or $p=1$ and $\gamma\in\mathbb R\setminus[-n,0]$ (resp. $\gamma\in\mathbb R\setminus[-1,0]$). We also prove that $\alpha_{p,\gamma}$ is sharp, and we establish exact limiting formulae and characterize Muckenhoupt weights via weak-type bounds. As applications, we characterize the weighted Hardy(--Sobolev) space $H^1_\upsilon$ with $\upsilon\in A_1$ in terms of the truncated Riesz transforms with optimal range $\gamma\in \mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$. More applications include the sharp weighted Caffarelli--Silvestre extension and the generalization to ball Banach function spaces.

papers.title: On transformations of Kamp\'e de F\'eriet functions with integral parameter differences
papers.abstract: We obtain analogues of the first Miller--Paris transformation for three classes of Kamp\'e de F\'eriet functions with unit parameter differences associated with the Appell function $F_1$. We also derive representations of the Appell function $F_1$ in terms of Kamp\'e de F\'eriet functions and reduction formulas expressing certain Kamp\'e de F\'eriet functions with integral parameter differences in terms of univariate generalized hypergeometric functions with integral parameter differences.

papers.title: The $C_p$ conjecture of Muckenhoupt
papers.abstract: We give an affirmative answer to Muckenhoupt's $C_p$ conjecture: for $1<p<\infty$, the $C_p$ condition is necessary and sufficient for the weighted $L^p(w)$ norm inequality relating the Hilbert transform and the Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator. We also show that the $C_p$ condition is necessary and sufficient for the weighted Fefferman--Stein inequality.

papers.title: Independent powers and bounded Fourier partial sums in $L^1$
papers.abstract: We construct a probability measure on the circle with independent convolution powers and uniformly bounded symmetric Fourier partial sums in $L^1$. Every positive convolution power is therefore singular with respect to Haar measure. The measure is Rajchman. The construction answers a question of Andersson concerning measures with bounded Fourier partial sums outside the radical of $L^1$, and contrasts with his theorem that the classical examples of Weiss, Katznelson, and Brown-Hewitt have convolution squares in $L^2$. Our proof combines sparse probability blocks, an endpoint $L\log L$ estimate, and a diagonal generalized Riesz product. Exact factorization of local moments permits the simultaneous separation of all convolution powers by Brown's singularity criterion. By the classical spectral theory of independent-power measures, its spectrum is the closed unit disc. In particular, it has non-natural spectrum and induces a non-decomposable convolution operator on $L^1$. The image of the measure in $M(\mathbb T)/L^1(\mathbb T)$ has spectral radius one, and the closed unital algebra it generates in $M(\mathbb T)$ is isometrically isomorphic to $\ell^1(\mathbb N_0)$.

papers.title: Sharp $L^p$--$L^q$ bounds for the strong circular maximal operator
papers.abstract: We study $L^p$--$L^q$ boundedness of the strong circular maximal operator $\M$, the maximal function over axis-parallel ellipses centered at the origin whose two semiaxes range independently over $[1,2]$. We prove that $\M$ is bounded from $L^p$ to $L^q$ whenever $(1/p,1/q)$ lies in the interior of the triangle with vertices $(0,0)$, $(2/7,1/7)$, and $(1/3,1/3)$, the two-parameter analogue of the triangle with vertices $(0,0)$, $(2/5,1/5)$, and $(1/2,1/2)$ obtained by Schlag and Schlag--Sogge for the circular maximal function. The range is sharp up to the boundary; in particular, weak type $(p,q)$ bounds fail for every $p\le3$. The proof is based on a bilinear estimate for frequencies in separated angular sectors, uniform as the sectors approach the coordinate axes. We also prove the analogous sharp result for axis dilations of a translated circle $c+\mathbb S^1$ with fixed $c\ne0$, where the vertex $(2/7,1/7)$ is replaced by $(1/4,1/8)$.

papers.title: Carleson duality and endpoint structure of Euclidean flag Triebel--Lizorkin spaces
papers.abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to develop the duality theory of the homogeneous Triebel--Lizorkin spaces associated with the Euclidean flag, using the discrete Littlewood--Paley--Stein analysis. After establishing bounded analysis and synthesis maps, we describe the continuous duals by Carleson conditions. In the Hardy spatial range, the representing distributions satisfy an open-set Carleson condition when the sequence exponent is greater than one and a coefficient supremum condition when the sequence exponent is at most one; in the Banach spatial range the dual is a conjugate-exponent or a supremum space. At the supremum sequence endpoint, the closure of the flag test functions is characterized by a pointwise scale tail measured in $L^p$, and a coefficient pairing decomposes every functional on the full space into a regular part and a part that annihilates the closure. By means of a fixed-envelope modulation construction we show that this closure is proper for every finite spatial exponent and that the annihilator is nonzero when the spatial exponent is at least one. The same analysis and synthesis framework also yields complex interpolation, real interpolation in the spatial exponent, the lifting property and the standard mixed-norm embeddings.

papers.title: Falconer estimate for circular and cinematic Furstenberg problem
papers.abstract: We prove the Falconer-type bound $\dim_{\mathrm H}F\geq u+1$ for planar circular $(u,v)$-Furstenberg sets whenever $0<u\leq1$, $0<v\leq3$, and $2u+v\geq3$. The same bound holds for smooth cinematic curve families. This resolves the circular Furstenberg conjecture of Green, Harris, Ou, Ren, and Tammen in its full Falconer range $2u+v\geq3$.

papers.title: Multilinear extrapolation on Banach function spaces
papers.abstract: We solve an open problem on the multilinear Rubio de Francia extrapolation on Banach function spaces. The first result states that, under the assumption of boundedness of the multisublinear Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, the multivariable boundedness on Banach function spaces can be extrapolated from some weighted Lebesgue space, including the cases where some exponents may be infinite. Under the same assumption, the second result asserts that if a multilinear operator is bounded on some weighted Lebesgue space, then its compactness can be extrapolated from some unweighted Lebesgue space to Banach function spaces. Our results do not require any convexity or concavity conditions on Banach function spaces. The main ingredients in the proof are a multilinear version of the Rubio de Francia algorithm, a stopping-time argument, convex analysis, and a compactness criterion on Banach function spaces. As applications of extrapolation theorems, we obtain multilinear extrapolation for the boundedness and compactness of commutators on Banach function spaces. These results can be further applied to specific operators, which cover both the full range case including multilinear Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund operators, multilinear pseudo-differential operators, and bilinear paraproducts, and the limited range case including the bilinear Hilbert transform, multilinear rough singular integrals, and bilinear oscillatory Fourier multipliers.

papers.title: Survey on Favard length and rectifiability
papers.abstract: We overview recent results quantifying the Besicovitch projection theorem, focusing on the theory of quantitative rectifiability and connection to Vitushkin's conjecture.

papers.title: Endpoint gradient bounds for centered convex maximal operators and probability kernels
papers.abstract: We establish the endpoint gradient estimate for centered homothetic maximal averages in every dimension $d\ge2$ over each fixed convex body with $C^{1,\theta}$ boundary, $0<\theta\le1$. In particular, the centered ball maximal operator satisfies the $W^{1,1}$ gradient bound in every dimension. Neither strict convexity nor a lower bound on the support gap is required. The geometric argument combines concentration in gradient values with nonhomogeneous calibrated rows and a summable radial correction. It extends the scalar refinement, direction-history construction and global assembly of the planar centered-disk proof of OpenAI. A separate transfer theorem gives sharp singular-derivative identities for bounded compact probability kernels once local BV output is known, and gradient continuity under an additional spatial-tail condition. Quantitative contact and translation estimates yield further profile and kernel examples. The estimates retain the fixed body's regularity data; the endpoint for arbitrary $C^1$ and nonsmooth convex bodies remains open here.

papers.title: Weak Hurwitz stability of extended Tur\'an expressions for Stirling--Whitney--Riordan and Laguerre polynomials
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a sufficient condition for weak Hurwitz stability of extended Tur\'an expressions for the Stirling--Whitney--Riordan polynomials. The proof uses polynomial transformations that preserve zeros in a real interval and in the unit disk. As an application, we prove that the extended Tur\'an expressions for the Bell polynomials are weakly Hurwitz stable. We also prove the corresponding result for the reflected Laguerre polynomials using polynomial approximations. These results settle two conjectures of Chasse, Grabarek, and Visontai.

papers.title: Attainable forms of intermediate dimensions of complementary sets
papers.abstract: Given a positive, non-increasing sequence $a$ with sum $1$, we consider the family $\mathcal{C}_a$ of closed subsets of $[0,1]$ whose complementary open intervals have lengths given by the terms of $a$. We study which functions $\theta\mapsto\overline{\dim}_{\,\theta}E$ arise as the upper intermediate dimensions of sets $E\in\mathcal{C}_a$. Under a natural condition on the decay of $a$, we show that these are exactly the functions in the class introduced by Banaji and Rutar that take the value $\overline{\dim}_{\rm B}C_a$ at $\theta=1$ and are bounded above by the upper intermediate dimensions of the decreasing Cantor set $C_a$. We also show that the lower bound given by the countable set $D_a$ is rigid: if it is attained at one value of $\theta$, then it is attained at all larger values.

papers.title: Rational limit of Rains integrals of type $A_n$
papers.abstract: We deduce the rational analogue of the elliptic Rains identity of type $A_n$ arXiv:0309252. We also derive reductions of the rational analogue and present the connection of them with well-known integrals in literature.

papers.title: Optimal Riesz mean inequalities for the Coulomb Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: We are interested in whether the Riesz means of the eigenvalues of the Coulomb Hamiltonian can be bounded by the corresponding semiclassical phase space integral. In dimensions two and three we determine the optimal Riesz exponent above which this bound holds.

papers.title: Geometric progressions in distance sets in odd dimensions over prime fields
papers.abstract: For $E\subset\mathbb{F}_p^d$, let $\Delta(E)=\{Q_d(x-y):x,y\in E\}$, where $Q_d(z)=z_1^2+\cdots+z_d^2$. We introduce and study the problem of the existence of nondegenerate three-term geometric progressions in the distance set $\Delta(E)$ when $d$ is odd. If $M_{GP,d}(p)$ denotes the largest size of a set whose distance set contains no such progression, then, for every prime $p\geq7$ and every integer $m\geq0$, \[ p^mM_{GP,1}(p)\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq4p^mM_{GP,1}(p). \] For all sufficiently large primes $p$, we also prove \[ p^{m+\frac{7}{26}}\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq Cp^{m+\frac{16}{25}}, \] where $C$ is an absolute positive constant.

papers.title: The estimates for Boolean surface area of polynomial threshold functions
papers.abstract: Polynomial threshold functions (PTFs) are an important low-complexity class of Boolean functions, with strong connections to learning theory and approximation theory. Recent work on learning and testing PTFs has exploited structural and isoperimetric properties of the class, especially bounds on average sensitivity, one of the central themes in the study of PTFs since the Gotsman--Linial conjecture recently solved by OpenAI, \cite{GLsol}. In this work we study PTFs through the lens of the Boolean surface area (or Talagrand boundary) \[ \mathbf{BSA}[f]=\mathbb{E}|\nabla f|=\mathbb{E}\sqrt{s_{f}(x)}, \] a natural measure of vertex-boundary complexity on the discrete cube. Our main result is that every degree-$d$ PTF has polylogarithmic Boolean surface area: \[ \mathbf{BSA}[f]\le C_d(\log(en))^{C_d}. \] The proof is based on the PTF Restriction Lemma of Kabanets, Kane, and Lu \cite{KKL2017} and proceeds through a tail bound for the pointwise sensitivity. In particular, it controls all subcritical fractional moments of the sensitivity. We also record a random block partition principle for Boolean surface area and an alternative recursive argument following Kane's work \cite{DK} on average sensitivity, which independently yields the second bound \[ \mathbf{BSA}[f]\le \exp(C(d)\sqrt{\log n}). \] This bound was obtained in \cite{FSVZ} without clarifying the magnitude of $C(d)$, which we do below. For lower moments $\bE |\nabla f|^{\eta} \le C(d, \eta)$ there is no dependence on $n$ for $0<\eta <1$.

papers.title: Fourier Ratio and Restricted Isometry via Entropic Descent
papers.abstract: In this second paper on descent methods as proof mechanisms in harmonic analysis (the first treated Bourgain's $\Lambda(p)$ selection theorem), entropic mirror descent gives an improved restricted isometry bound, improving sampling and recovery bounds in the Fourier Ratio program. Let $H$ be a complex $n\times n$ matrix with $H^*H=nI$ and $|H_{ij}|=1$. For fixed $0<\varepsilon<\frac14$ and $A_0>0$, independent Bernoulli row selection with expected cardinality $C_{\varepsilon,A_0}r\log\frac{2en}{r}\log(2r)\leq m\leq n/2$ preserves, after normalization by $\sqrt m$, the squared norm of every complex vector $y$ with $\|y\|_1\leq\sqrt r\|y\|_2$ within a factor $1\pm\varepsilon$, with failure probability at most $Cn^{-A_0}$. This includes every $r$-sparse vector and also fully supported ones; support size enters only through this inequality. For $y=\widehat f$ the condition is exactly $\operatorname{FR}(f)^2\leq r$, where $\operatorname{FR}(f)=\|\widehat f\|_1/\|\widehat f\|_2$, giving uniform energy sampling and approximate recovery even for signals with full Fourier support. The same holds for a uniform subset of prescribed cardinality, and for discrete Fourier and real Hadamard matrices. At fixed accuracy the bound removes one sparsity logarithm from the earlier count and replaces $\log n$ by $\log\frac{2en}{r}$; for Walsh matrices it matches, up to constants, the lower bound of B\l asiok et al.\ in their range. One relative-entropy potential controls the corrections of an amplitude predictor at every scale; counting them on the symmetric difference of two samples gives the uniform estimate. We also prove the sufficient bound $C_{A_0}\varepsilon^{-5}r\log\frac{2en}{r}\log\frac{2r}{\varepsilon}$, and stable sparse recovery from $Cs\log\frac{2en}{s}\log(2s)$ measurements, with error controlled by the noise and the best $s$-term approximation.

papers.title: Sharp noncommutative Hilbert and Riesz inequalities: classification and spectral corrections
papers.abstract: For every $1<p<\infty$, with $p^*=\max\{p,p/(p-1)\}$, we determine the sharp Hilbert norm $C_p=\cot(\pi/(2p^*))$ on $L^p(\mathbb{R};\mathcal{S}_p)$ and the sharp uniform bound $D_p=\csc(\pi/p)$ for retained and strict Riesz projections of maximal subdiagonal algebras in finite tracial von Neumann algebras. The Hilbert value is also the common Fourier--Schur completely bounded norm. For finite matrices, a nonnegative logarithmic determinant defect connects Hein\"avaara's tracial joint spectral measure to eigenvalues. The resulting transfer identity classifies finite signed real ridge inequalities on nilpotents and identifies their least additive eigenvalue corrections. A dual theorem characterizes weak-* limits of weighted angular measures of finite nilpotents. In general finite tracial algebras, separate positive-kernel and sharp determinant-covariance comparisons yield the Riesz bounds. Consequences include the sharp Volterra constant, Riesz--Titchmarsh and shifted-transform formulas, joint real-pencil norms, and exact triangular and operator-valued Fourier Riesz norms.

papers.title: Projection Theorems in the Presence of Expansions
papers.abstract: We prove a restricted projection theorem for a certain one dimensional family of projections from $\mathbb R^n$ to $\mathbb R^k$. The family we consider here arises naturally in the study of quantitative equidistribution problems in homogeneous dynamics.

papers.title: Hausdorff content $A_p$ weights: weighted maximal inequalities and fundamental structural properties
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal H_{\infty}^\delta$ denote the Hausdorff content of dimension $\delta\in(0,n]$ defined on subsets of $\mathbb R^n$. The principal problem, considered in this paper, is to characterize the non-negative function $w$ for which the weighted $L^p$ inequality with $p\in(1,\infty)$ and the weighted weak $L^1$ inequality on Hardy-Littlewood maximal operators associated with Hausdorff content hold true. To achieve this, we introduce a class of Hausdorff content $A_p$ weights, denoted as $\mathcal A_{p,\delta}$, and then show that, for any $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $\delta\in(0,n]$, the weighted $L^p$ maximal inequality holds true if and only if $w\in\mathcal A_{p,\delta}$, and the weighted weak $L^1$ maximal inequality holds true if and only if $w\in\mathcal A_{1,\delta}$ by proposing a novel approach. As the second objective, applying this approach, the seminal structural properties of classical Muckenhoupt $A_p$ weights, such as the reverse H\"older inequality [R. R. Coifman and C. Fefferman, Studia Math. 51 (1974), 241-250], the self-improving property [B. Muckenhoupt, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 165 (1972), 207-226], and Jones' factorization theorem [P. W. Jones, Ann. of Math. (2) 111 (1980), 511-530], are all established for $\mathcal A_{p,\delta}$. The main novelties of this paper lies in: (i) we discover $\mathcal A_{p,\delta}$ weights with rich structural properties, that increase strictly on dimension exponent and hence reduce to the classical $A_p$ class at the endpoint dimension, forming proper subsets of it for smaller dimension exponent; (ii) by proposing a novel approach, this work naturally extends the classical theory beyond measure-theoretic frameworks, while also provides novel insights even when reduced to the classical $A_p$ weight case.

papers.title: A note on characterization of $H^1$ Sobolev spaces by square functions
papers.abstract: We establish characterization of $H^1$ Sobolev spaces by certain square functions, improving previous results.

papers.title: Fractional Besov-Sobolev Spaces on Chord-arc Curves
papers.abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a bounded rectifiable Jordan curve, with complementary domains $\Omega_i$ and $\Omega_e$. For $1<p<\infty$ and $0<s<1$, we study the spaces $\mathcal B_{p,p}^s(\Omega)$ of harmonic functions satisfying \[ \iint_\Omega |\nabla u(z)|^p \operatorname{dist}(z,\Gamma)^{(1-s)p-1}\,dA(z)<\infty, \qquad \Omega\in\{\Omega_i,\Omega_e\}. \] When $\Gamma$ is the unit circle, the traces of these two spaces coincide with the fractional Besov-Sobolev space $B^s_{p,p}(\Gamma)$. The equivalence of boundary seminorms and harmonic energies on the circle raises a geometric question: which rough curves preserve these estimates? For every radial-Lipschitz curve $\Gamma$, we prove \[ \operatorname{Tr}_\Gamma\mathcal B_{p,p}^s(\Omega_i) =B_{p,p}^s(\Gamma) =\operatorname{Tr}_\Gamma\mathcal B_{p,p}^s(\Omega_e) \] whenever either $1 < p < 2$ and $2/p - 1 \leq s < 1$, $2 < p < \infty$ and $0 < s \leq 1/2 + 1/p$ or $p=2$ and $0<s<1$. For arbitrary chord-arc curves, the same trace identities hold when $1/p\le s<1/2+1/(2p)$. Taking $s=1-1/p$ yields an almost-Dirichlet principle for the unweighted $p$-energy on radial-Lipschitz domains when $3/2\le p\le4$. Here, the upper bound $4$ is sharp. In particular, every Riemann map $g:\Omega_i\to\mathbb D_i$ from a bounded radial-Lipschitz domain satisfies $g'\in L^4(\Omega_i)$, and the exponent $4$ is optimal uniformly over this class. This gives a sharp endpoint counterpart of Brennan's integrability conclusion for radial-Lipschitz domains.

papers.title: Two Hornich-Hlawka-type and Gram matrix-based inequalities
papers.abstract: We establish two inequalities in real inner product spaces. The first is a multiplicative strengthening of the classical Hornich-Hlawka inequality: for all vectors $x,y,z$ in a real inner product space $H$, \[ \|x\|\,\|y\| + \|z\|\,\|x+y+z\| \;\geq\; \|x+z\|\,\|y+z\|.\] We provide a complete characterization of the equality cases. The second result is a parametric inequality derived from the positive semidefiniteness of Gram matrices: for all $x,y,z \in H$ and $\alpha, \beta, \gamma \in \mathbb{R}$, \[ \alpha^2\|x\|^2\langle y,z\rangle^2 + \beta^2\|y\|^2\langle x,z\rangle^2 + \gamma^2\|z\|^2\langle x,y\rangle^2 + 2(\alpha\beta + \alpha\gamma + \beta\gamma)\langle x,y\rangle\langle x,z\rangle\langle y,z\rangle \;\geq\; 0 \], which, upon optimization over the parameters yields sharp reverse inequalities to the Gram determinant inequality $\det G \geq 0$. As a special case, this recovers and strengthens the classical Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.

papers.title: Time-periodic carrying simplex for a competitive system of Carath\'eodory ODEs
papers.abstract: We establish the existence of a time-periodic carrying simplex for competitive systems of Kolmogorov-type ordinary differential equations of the form $\dot{x}_i = x_i g_i(t,x)$, $i=1,\dots,d$, on $\mathbb{R}^d_+$, where the vector field $g$ is $T$-periodic in time and satisfies only Carath\'eodory conditions rather than the classical $C^1$ regularity assumed in earlier work. We show that the time-$T$ Poincar\'e map $P$ generated by the flow is retrotone, and apply recent results on the carrying simplex for retrotone maps to obtain for $P$ a carrying simplex $\Sigma$ that is an unordered, Lipschitz, invariant manifold homeomorphic to the standard probability simplex, and that attracts all nonzero trajectories of the discrete dynamical system generated by $P$. We then extend this construction to the full nonautonomous flow by introducing an auxiliary autonomous system on the extended phase space $\mathcal{T} \times \mathbb{R}^d_+$, where $\mathcal{T}$ is the circle of length $T$, generated via a skew-product formulation. In the context of this extended phase space we then construct a compact global attractor and identify, as its relative boundary, a time-periodic family of carrying simplices $\{\Sigma_s\}_{s \in \mathcal{T}}$ that depend continuously on the phase $s$, each homeomorphic to the standard simplex and each attracting, uniformly in $s$, all nonzero orbits of the corresponding time-shifted flow. These results provide a rigorous foundation for the qualitative analysis of seasonally forced competitive population models in which growth rates need only be measurable and locally Lipschitz in time, broadening the applicability of carrying simplex theory to more realistic ecological settings.
